title: A stop signal that arrives while the release writes its live record still stops the release command
objective: Once core.release.run has started the release command, an exception raised before the command's wait ends never leaves the command running.
outline: devloop/core/release.py run(): today the `try:` whose `except BaseException: osx.kill_tree(proc.pid); raise` stops the command wraps only `osx.wait(...)`, and the `inflight.put(cfg, live_name, {...})` of the command's record sits between `proc = osx.spawn(...)` and that `try:`. Move that `inflight.put(...)` call (with the dict built in its arguments: osx.host(), osx.boot_id(), osx.now()) inside the `try:`, so the `try:` begins on the statement right after `proc = osx.spawn(...)`. The except clause stays exactly as it is; its comment may say that a signal or a failed live-record write stops the command too (see notes for words to avoid). An OSFailure from the put then stops the command and re-raises to the outer `except osx.OSFailure`, which already appends it to the log and returns (False, text). Nothing else changes: devloop/release_job.py, devloop/core/osx.py and devloop/core/inflight.py stay untouched. Measured in a scratch clone of 147c47b: exactly this 4-line move turns the three acceptance cases from red to green and keeps the 29 existing cases of test_release.T142Acceptance, test_release.ReleaseJobUnit and test_machine.ReleaseTakesWhatARegressionTakes green (32 cases with the new ones, 40 s).

notes:
Cause (measured). In core.release.run the command's live record is written by inflight.put between osx.spawn and the try whose except stops the command. inflight.put does an fsync'd atomic write and then scans every live record; /tmp, where the loop tests live, is on /dev/vda, and the g20 regression ran 30 shards on 4 CPUs, so that write can outlast the shell's start, and T142 item9's SIGTERM (sent as soon as the command wrote its pid file) can land inside it. agents.Interrupted then propagates past the guard: release_job.py writes 'stopped by SIGTERM; the release command was stopped' and exits 2 while the command keeps running - exactly the regression failure (the rc 2 assertion passed, the 5 s 'process was stopped' wait failed; shard-6 log of int-g20). Reproduced deterministically on 147c47b in a scratch clone with acceptance 3's fixture: rc 2, --out written, the sleep still alive after 5 s; acceptance 1 and 2 red too. In production the same window lets a release stopped by the controller keep running in a worktree that run()'s finally has already removed, after its job reported it stopped.
Hypotheses. H1 (above): measured, this ticket. H2: item9's oracle waits on PID 1 to reap the stopped sleep (osx.alive counts another process's unreaped zombie as alive); measured reaping 1.0-2.0 s after the end on this machine, idle and with 12 CPU-bound loops on 4 CPUs - inside the 5 s window, so not the cause unless PID 1 stalls over 3 s (not measured under the regression's I/O load); not changed here, and the reason case 3 allows 10 s. H3: pid reuse within 5 s - not measured, implausible with Linux pid space.
Out of scope. (a) The remaining window inside osx.spawn (from the fork until it returns the Popen): a signal there loses the Popen; closing it needs signal masking around the spawn in core/osx.py, which ticket #147 (stuck on hard_block, no group) also edits, and the test cannot hit it unless the job is descheduled for the whole shell start plus the test's 50 ms poll. (b) Do not edit T142 item9: the request forbids hiding the flake in the test, and item9 is green with the move (its cleanup osx.kill_tree(rel_pid) cannot reach a process that is not a group leader, harmless once the command is stopped). (c) core/agents.py keeps self.proc and stops it in stop(), a different shape; regression.py is #147's subject. Neither changes.
hard_block words: keep every added line (code, comments, docstrings, tests, shell strings) free of `os.kill`, `killpg`, `pkill` and `kill -`. In tests stop leftovers only with osx.kill_tree(...) or Popen.kill() and check liveness only with osx.alive; in comments write 'stop the process group'. The moved lines contain none of them.
Group: no open group exists (g21 is pr and takes no new tickets; g20 has landed), so a new group new-g1 at the end of the chain, no dependencies. Files: devloop/core/release.py and tests_devloop/test_release.py only; #147's outline touches core/osx.py and scripts/testiface.py - no overlap.
acceptance: In-process, board config devloop.machine_slots null and release `sleep 30`: when `core.inflight.put` (patched as `release.inflight.put`) raises `agents.Interrupted("signal 15")`, `release.run(Config(proj), {"id": "g1", "members": ["1"]}, sha)` raises that same `agents.Interrupted`, and when it reaches the caller the process that `core.osx.spawn` started for the command is no longer running (`osx.alive(pid)` is False).

Same fixture, `release.inflight.put` raises `osx.OSFailure("cannot write the live record")`: `release.run` returns `(False, "cannot write the live record")` (as today) and the process `osx.spawn` started is no longer running when it returns.

devloop/release_job.py with machine_slots null, release command `echo $$ > G; sleep 60 & echo $! > P.tmp; mv P.tmp P; wait` (G, P: files in the test's tmp dir) and its live-record write held open by a fake `core.inflight.put` that sleeps 30 s before writing: a SIGTERM sent once P exists makes it exit 2 within 10 s with --out holding ok false, signal "SIGTERM", text "stopped by SIGTERM; the release command was stopped" and sha equal to --sha, and within 10 s after that exit the background process whose pid is in P is no longer running (`osx.alive` False).

Seams the cases patch stay as they are today: release.run starts the command with `osx.spawn` from core.osx and writes the command's live record with `inflight.put` from core.inflight, once, after `osx.spawn` returns; release_job.py still calls `release.run` and keeps `main(argv)`.

Unchanged (the implementer's own run; no new case, these hold today): test_release.T142Acceptance (item9 included), test_release.ReleaseJobUnit and test_machine.ReleaseTakesWhatARegressionTakes pass without edits. They pin: without slots one `inflight.put` whose stamp pid is the command's; with regression_exclusive the puts are stage "machine" then the command's; a wait interrupted by KeyboardInterrupt stops the command with one `osx.kill_tree` call; rc 0 returns (True, log tail); rc N returns "rc N[ (timeout)]" plus the tail; an OSFailure before the spawn (worktree, slot) returns its text.
